title: Distributed Job Scheduler
summary: Run millions of one-off and cron jobs on time and at least once: a durable job store indexed by run time, partitioned schedulers that claim due jobs with leases, a work queue, idempotent workers, retries and visibility.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Submit a job to run now, at a time, or on a cron schedule
Retries with backoff, timeouts, cancellation; view status and history
Jobs start within ~1–2 s of their scheduled time
At-least-once execution; no job silently lost

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Cron jobs cluster on round times (every hour at :00). Plan for the top-of-the-hour spike, and jitter where the user allows it.

POST /jobs {name, payload, schedule: "0 * * * *" | run_at, max_retries, timeout_s, idempotency_key}
GET  /jobs/{id}            -> definition + next_run_at
GET  /jobs/{id}/runs       -> [{run_id, status, started_at, attempts, error}]
POST /jobs/{id}/cancel

blocks.caption: Store → claim due jobs → queue → workers

sections.title: Deep dive: claiming due jobs exactly once (mostly)

items.title: Partition
items.text: Jobs are hashed into N partitions; each scheduler instance owns a set of partitions via leader election / leases (ZooKeeper, etcd, or a DB lease table).

items.title: Poll
items.text: Every second: SELECT jobs WHERE partition IN (mine) AND next_run_at <= now() ORDER BY next_run_at LIMIT 1000 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

items.title: Enqueue
items.text: Create a run row and push to the work queue; compute and store the next next_run_at for cron jobs in the same transaction.

items.title: Execute
items.text: Workers take a visibility timeout / lease on the run, heartbeat while running, mark success or failure.

items.title: Recover
items.text: If a heartbeat stops, the run becomes visible again and is retried — hence at-least-once and idempotent jobs.

blocks.text:
SELECT id FROM jobs
 WHERE partition = ANY($1) AND next_run_at <= now() AND status = 'scheduled'
 ORDER BY next_run_at
 LIMIT 1000
 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: For far-future timers at huge scale, a **timing wheel** or bucketed time index (jobs grouped per minute) avoids scanning a giant sorted index.

items: Scheduler shard dies → its lease expires → another instance takes the partitions (a few seconds of delay).
Duplicate execution is possible (lease expiry while still running) — require idempotency keys or fencing tokens for side effects.
Retries: exponential backoff with jitter; poison jobs go to a dead-letter queue after max attempts.
Separate queues per priority/tenant to prevent one tenant's 1M-job burst from starving others.

cols.title: DB polling
cons: Index hot spot at now(); polling cost

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The store is the source of truth for when; the queue is just the hand-off for who. Leases plus idempotent workers give at-least-once without losing jobs.

items.q: How do you support DAGs of jobs?
items.a: That's a workflow engine: persist each step's state and trigger children on completion (Airflow, Temporal).

items.q: How do you cancel a running job?
items.a: Set a cancel flag; workers check it on heartbeat and stop; the scheduler won't enqueue future runs.
Not across arbitrary side effects; at-least-once + idempotency (or transactional outbox) is the practical answer.

items: Index on next_run_at; partitions owned by scheduler leases.
